approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored current molecule by sampling local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including direct formula-preserving exchanges of aromatic nitrogen and carbon positions. It sanitizes and normalizes each molecular identity, rejects duplicates, and submits the first full batch permitted by short-lived inverse-motif memory. It moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening move and keeps its best observation separately. A veto needs opposite signed motif matches from one earlier selected transition, but a recurring signed motif currently transfers its sole memory entry to the newest transition.
approach.novelty: Preserve overlapping transition provenance: let the same inverse motif retain a separate, independently expiring entry for each recent selected transition that installed it. A newer use can then coexist with an older pair through the older pair's original lifetime. This tests whether preserving coherent short-term protection redirects evaluations usefully. Earlier siblings withheld credit after nonimproving moves or required a complete signature match; this change retains unconditional credit and the existing two-sign predicate while changing only how overlapping origins survive.

observed_bottleneck: The complete Parent n-abcd951ab7cc has macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population standard deviation 0.006329100643035156. Its latest-origin table overwrites 46 still-live restrictions across 37 installation events and 12 of 15 task sessions. The overwritten entries are only one, two or three completed steps old, in counts 16, 19 and 11, despite nominal four-step tenure. Four affected older groups lose their last available sign or disappear. Independent chronological reconstruction from the actual Parent logs reproduces all 1711 installations, 435 selected transitions and 195 vetoes among 4545 valid novel draws. Retaining every installation until its original expiry on that identical accepted history preserves additional qualifying origins on three draws: two already vetoed draws remain vetoed, while one formerly admitted draw becomes vetoed, giving 196 vetoes. The newly blocked historical example is an aromatic nitrogen relocation in deco_hop seed 1, batch 4, attempt 43; it improved its source by 0.0002621083644149813 but was neither an archive improvement nor the selected next state. Thus early provenance loss and a resulting admission are demonstrated, while their score harm is unproved and exposure is sparse. The credit-gating sibling n-a240f72e3717 independently showed a preserved older pair causing an extra veto, yet lost 0.020273360127168 in paired mean. The complete-signature sibling n-7c411fdf5a88 also activated and lost 0.039186838732539676. These negative results argue against treating fewer vetoes or occasional useful admissions as sufficient evidence; the present question is whether older transition protection should survive a later overlapping installation.
hypothesis: Retain a separate inverse-motif restriction for every still-live selected-transition provenance when signed motif keys overlap, so later installations do not overwrite older provenance and the unchanged same-transition bidirectional veto can use each origin until its own original expiry or documented oldest-entry release.

finding_summary.headline: Older motif provenance changed one evaluated batch and its winner, but the final score fell
finding_summary.insights: Premature overwrite can remove a restriction that later matters to an admission decision, so preserving origins does more than increase table occupancy. Yet the opportunities were sparse: 47 collision pairings across 36 installation events yielded only one changed complete batch. The parent and child each recorded 195 vetoes in total, showing why whole-run veto counts alone would have missed this activation. The newly available replacement was locally better and won its batch, but its subsequent walk ended worse. Immediate source or archive gains therefore do not establish useful long-term redirection, and the later loss cannot be treated as the isolated value of the excluded molecule. This narrows the result to coherent short-term provenance protection; it does not establish that shared local motifs identify reversal of an entire edit or that broader retention improves search. The molecular assessment also finds the inherited aromatic and ring-rich families, unusual sulfur bonding, reactive decorations and unspecified stereochemistry largely intact, with no demonstrated chemistry improvement explaining the redirection. The benefit under histories with more overlap-dependent candidates remains open. No obstruction release occurred, so behavior after a release was not tested.
finding_summary.results: Across the 15 task-and-seed sessions, 45 older restrictions survived overlapping installations without losing their original provenance or expiry. They preserved four bidirectional transition groups that the latest-origin rule would have broken. On the same accepted histories, this produced one additional veto among 4,545 valid novel candidate tests; two other tests gained an older qualifying origin but were already vetoed. The extra veto changed one complete ten-molecule batch in deco_hop seed 1. Its replacement was evaluated, beat the source by 0.004805, became the next state and immediately raised the best observed score by 0.002352. Nevertheless, this seed finished at 0.594191 versus the parent's 0.605140. All 14 other trajectories were unchanged. The three-seed macro mean was 0.521029 versus 0.521759, a paired change of -0.000730 against the required +0.002. Across all 4,350 accepted proposals, the source-beating frequency fell from 10.759% to 10.621%, and strict archive improvements fell from 238 to 232. Provenance retention and evaluation redirection are confirmed; the specified score-benefit claim is refuted.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families persist, with unusual sulfur bonding, reactive decorations and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: The generated set spans moderately sized fused heteroaryl amides and ketones, larger decorated nitrogenous heterocycles, aminoalkyl polycycles, and densely connected sulfur-containing cages. Every covered task has 870 optimizer proposals and ring_closure_rate 1.0. Aromatic-atom presence rates range from 0.7184 to 1.0; these are fractions of strings containing aromatic notation, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths range from 46.2 to 69.9 and describe textual complexity, not molecular weight. Conventional aromatic/carbonyl substructures remain recognizable, but many higher-scoring molecules combine them with heteroatom-halogen bonds, unusual multiply bonded sulfur, or elaborate bridges. Thus synthetic plausibility is questionable overall, although the simpler indole carboxamides look substantially more conventional than the sulfur cages. Structural diversity is moderate across the observed families, with close analogues concentrated within each seed; numerous unique strings do not establish broad useful scaffold coverage. All panels report stereocentre_rate 0.0 and charged_rate 0.0. This shows absent explicit stereochemical and charge notation; it does not show absent stereogenic atoms or absent basic amines. All supplied Child and Parent trajectory records agree outside deco_hop seed 1. The chemistry therefore largely persists from Parent n-abcd951ab7cc. All objectives listed in the brief have trajectories; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The readings below concern observed molecular-score associations and apparent chemistry, without assigning biological activity, synthetic routes, objective components, or mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: Moderately sized, substituted fused heteroaromatics predominate: indole carboxanilides, benzofuran carboxanilides and benzothiophene aryl ketones, carrying alkoxy, methyl, amino, thiol and halogen-containing substituents. The later stream also contains enlarged, partly dearomatized bridged rings. Mean SMILES length is 46.2, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9563 and halogen_rate 0.7552. The ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide at seed 1 evaluation 61 is a recognizable medicinal-chemistry framework; the seed 2 best adds an N-chloroamide and an amino/chloro-substituted benzylic carbon, making its plausibility more doubtful. All trajectories and best structures match the Parent.
liabilities: N-chloroamide, N-fluoro/N-hydroxy amine and benzylic halide motifs introduce apparent reactivity concerns beyond the ordinary heteroaryl amide framework.
Dense partly dearomatized bridges and multiply bonded sulfur appear in late molecules without stereochemical specification or evidence of a feasible synthesis.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the favorable compact aromatic-carbonyl arrangement is missing from low-scoring ring-expansion and carbonyl-disruption proposals.

A demonstrated set of conventional analogues retaining the best benzofuran substitution pattern while replacing its N-chloroamide and amino/chloro carbon is missing; the scores do not establish those reactive decorations as necessary.
The shown gradient does not identify a particular unobserved target-specific functional group as the missing answer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-substituted indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145, compared with 0.39905049777278273 for the ethoxy/methyl/thiol analogue and 0.41003927643747895 for the substituted benzofuran N-chloroamide. The benzothiophene aryl ketone also reaches 0.393567030299894. In contrast, the indole derivative in which the carbonyl linkage is replaced by a substituted saturated amino linkage scores 0.03343008011310944; a much less aromatic enlarged-ring ketone scores 0.021532846118034143. These comparisons associate the better region with intact fused aromatic/carbonyl/aryl arrangements and selective peripheral changes. They do not isolate a benefit from N-chlorination, thiols or any single substituent. The dense later ring systems can retain appreciable scores, so neither maximum aromaticity nor simple synthetic appearance is a sufficient explanation.

per_task.generated_character: These are large, heavily decorated nitrogen-rich aromatic heterocycles with carbonyl or thiocarbonyl groups. The strongest seed 0 family carries a substituted phenyl group, exocyclic imines, an amino/fluoro carbon linker, and an extended ether/thioether/acetal-like appendage attached through unusual multiply bonded sulfur. Late seed 2 examples retain a fused dicarbonyl heterocycle with polyenyl and bulky alkoxy substituents. Mean SMILES length is 69.3, maximum length 95, and aromatic_atom_rate 1.0. The conventional heterocyclic cores are recognizable, but the accumulated decorations make the complete structures synthetically questionable. Only seed 1 differs from the Parent: its observed best is an expanded nitrogen-rich carbonyl/imine heterocycle with an alkenyl side chain and an aryl thioacyl group, while the Parent best has heteroaryl-linked amidine and thioester functionality. Neither family establishes a cleaner chemical solution.
liabilities: The best family combines terminal imines, N-bromination, unusual sulfur bonding and long heteroatom-rich appendages; nearby leaders also carry sulfur-chlorine bonds.
Flexible ether/thioether/acetal-like chains and crowded substituent patterns increase synthetic and conformational uncertainty. No synthesis or stability evidence accompanies these scores.
missing_features: A demonstrated economical representation of the higher-scoring heterocyclic arrangement is missing: closely related enlarged appendages receive identical scores, leaving the minimal useful attachment pattern unresolved.
Conventional, tractable replacements for the multiply bonded sulfur linkage and reactive terminal groups are not established among the leading examples.
The lower-scoring changed seed does not establish which lost or relocated heteroaryl feature caused the decrease, because its scaffold and substituents changed together.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623. A lower optimizer example with a reorganized nonaromatic fused nitrogen ring scores 0.526081691583997, whereas the elaborated seed 0 thione/oxo family reaches 0.6161710037174721. Several cited decorated analogues share exactly 0.6155070237050044 despite changes in alkyl length, sulfur substitution or N-bromination. The local plateau therefore supplies no evidence that each added decoration contributes. The changed seed 1 trajectory ends at best_so_far 0.5941905687894993 versus Parent 0.605139548855754; these seed-specific best structures are described from the full trajectories and are not quoted because they are outside the supplied digest. The observed gradient favors particular reorganizations and decorations of the inherited heterocyclic family, but it does not reveal the unseen structural requirement of the objective.

per_task.generated_character: Large halogenated aromatic/polycyclic molecules evolve from carboxylic-acid, amide and sulfonamide-rich starting chemistry toward unacylated cyclic amines, aminomethyl substituents, phenols and aryl groups linked through unusual sulfur-containing rings. The best seed 2 structure combines a phenolic aryl group, a chlorophenyl group, an aminomethyl-substituted N/S ring and a bridged amine-containing sulfur framework. Seed 0 leaders include small saturated aza rings and sulfur-rich aryl linkages. Mean SMILES length is 69.9, aromatic_atom_rate 1.0 and halogen_rate 0.9966. Free amine centres are present despite charged_rate 0.0. The aromatic/amine functionality is medicinally recognizable, but sulfur-sulfur multiple bonding and dense asymmetric ring systems make the full structures questionable. Every trajectory matches the Parent.
liabilities: Multiply bonded sulfur with explicit sulfur hydrogens, sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and cumulated heteroatom bonding appear in high-scoring structures, raising strong synthetic plausibility questions.
Halogen-heavy aromatic regions, crowded aza rings and unspecified stereochemistry complicate interpretation of the proposed shapes and functional-group presentation.
missing_features: Conventional analogues preserving the favorable amine-to-aromatic connectivity and spacer geometry without unusual sulfur-sulfur or carbon-sulfur multiple bonding are not demonstrated.

Explicit stereochemical alternatives and plausible charge-state representations are absent despite asymmetric saturated rings and free amines; their effect on this score cannot be inferred from the shown molecules.
Lower-scoring proposals fail to preserve the specific aminoalkyl attachment and distal aromatic structure that the local comparisons support.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An early acid/amide/sulfonamide-containing optimizer molecule scores 0.007468397818197266, while the phenolic aminoalkyl sulfur polycycle reaches 0.9148143511682032. A closely related aminomethyl-containing structure scores 0.8663008496126992; replacing one aminomethyl branch with an aminooxy branch gives 0.5308080684367313, removing a methylene between a ring nitrogen and the sulfur-containing ring gives 0.3331237338421948, and disrupting its distal chlorophenyl ring with sulfur gives 0.04252669549740123. These local comparisons support sensitivity to aminoalkyl connectivity, linker spacing and an intact distal aromatic group. They do not show that adding more nitrogen is uniformly beneficial or that the exotic sulfur framework is required. The high recorded score is not direct evidence of binding, selectivity, stability or synthesizability.

per_task.generated_character: Medium-to-large aryl/heteroaryl polycycles carry tertiary lactam or related carbonyl groups, alkyl substituents and bridged nitrogen/oxygen linkages. The best excerpt is concentrated on an azaaryl/aryl unsaturated bridged scaffold containing an N-O bond and a cyclic carbonyl-containing chain. Other seeds explore brominated aryl/thioester families and later sulfur-rich bridged carbonyl structures. Mean SMILES length is 61.0 and aromatic_atom_rate 1.0. Aromatic rings and carbonyl functionality are abundant; the unusual bridges and heteroatom bonds make the overall chemistry questionable rather than obviously tractable. The complete trajectories match the Parent.
liabilities: N-O and N-N bridges, including a peroxide-containing high-scoring analogue, give uncertain stability and synthesis compared with ordinary lactam scaffolds.
Other proposals carry oxygen-bromine bonds and unusual sulfur substituents; late sulfur-rich cages retain scores without resolving these chemical concerns.
Asymmetric bridged structures have no explicit stereochemical specification.
missing_features: Several independent, conventional ring/linker arrangements reproducing the favorable aryl, heteroaryl and carbonyl placement are not established; the leading digest remains concentrated on a bridged N-O family.
A demonstrated compact and tractable alternative to the elaborate bridges is missing. Additional rings alone are not the missing chemistry, because ring closure is already universal.
The shown scores do not establish which unobserved functional group would satisfy the objective beyond the local topology and substituent associations.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. Ring-opened derivatives bearing pendant amino/carbonyl chains score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515, while the bridged azaaryl/aryl lactam family reaches 0.21196904390980506. A close ring-expanded/phenyl analogue scores 0.2108231310031427, and a peroxide-containing related bridge remains at 0.20647766243219587. The gradient is consistent with a particular constrained aryl/heteroatom/carbonyl arrangement and tolerates substantial changes in the tether chemistry. The modest separation from the median 0.17833 does not identify an unseen target motif, and near-top tolerance of the peroxide bridge does not endorse its chemical quality.

per_task.generated_character: Compact but highly connected heteroatom-rich polycycles replace much of the initial peripheral aryl chemistry. The leading seed 1 molecules retain a nitrogenous dicarbonyl/[nH] region embedded in dense sulfur-containing fused and bridged rings, with carbon-fluorine substituents and a sulfur-linked fluorinated alcohol branch. Other seeds reach sulfur-rich carbonyl cages carrying an acyl fluoride, or an aldehyde and N-fluoro imino functionality. Mean SMILES length is 62.8, aromatic_atom_rate 0.7184 and halogen_rate 0.7. This is rich ring chemistry with less persistent aromatic notation than the other panels, not an absence of rings. The tightly interlocked sulfur frameworks look particularly difficult to realize as conventional stable molecules. All trajectories match the Parent.
liabilities: Dense ring intersections and multiple unusual carbon-sulfur and sulfur-sulfur bond environments make synthetic plausibility especially weak for the leading cages.

The seed 0 leading excerpt contains an acyl fluoride; late seed 2 examples contain N-F functionality, an aldehyde, and a sulfur-chlorine acyl derivative. These are apparent reactivity liabilities, not evidence of a stable medicinal scaffold.
No explicit stereochemistry resolves the asymmetric saturated ring junctions or substituted fluorinated carbons.
missing_features: Conventional heterocyclic or partially saturated scaffolds presenting the favorable compact fluorinated carbonyl/donor arrangement without the elaborate sulfur network are not demonstrated among the leaders.
Specified stereochemistry is missing from highly asymmetric fluorinated cages; neither a preferred stereoisomer nor a score benefit from assigning one can be inferred.
The demonstrated gradient concerns compactness and heteroatom placement within unusual cages; it does not justify prescribing an unobserved objective-specific group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.0020944534688323298, and an early expanded carbonyl-containing derivative scores 7.590554525032884e-10. The compact fluorinated sulfur cage reaches 0.5903526424693334. In the late seed 2 series, a compact sulfur/carbonyl cage scores 0.4484554129767839, whereas an analogue with expanded carbon paths scores 0.01685401516576383. Within these observed families the better region is associated with compact connectivity, fluorination and reorganized heteroatom/carbonyl placement. Several features change together, and low-scoring sulfur-rich examples show that sulfur addition alone is insufficient. The observations do not identify a required reference-like pharmacophore or establish any reward for chemical stability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Higher-scoring digest molecules contain N-chloroamides, N-brominated heterocycles, N-F groups, multiply bonded sulfur with explicit sulfur hydrogens, and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds. Recognizable aromatic, carbonyl and amine fragments coexist with these liabilities. Some chemically more conventional analogues score well, so none of these liabilities is demonstrated to be universally necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve conventional local chemical environments while varying favorable ring and linker arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could expose alternatives with conventional bond environments while preserving the surrounding attachments, using local chemical context rather than atom valence alone. Evaluate such alternatives through the existing score interface; a plausibility preference is a hypothesis to test, not an assumed score improvement or a blanket exclusion of sulfur.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading examples concentrate on close analogues of fused heteroaryl carbonyls, N-O bridged azaaryl lactams, aminoalkyl sulfur polycycles and dense fluorinated cages. Low-scoring counterparts often disrupt an aromatic ring, carbonyl linkage or aminoalkyl spacer; the output does not establish that elaborate bridges are required to retain the favorable arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks demonstrated simple scaffold and linker alternatives that retain favorable functional-group placement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemically coherent ring/linker replacements or simplifications that retain attachment points and recognizable donor, acceptor and aromatic arrangements. Such proposals would test whether the same useful local features can be expressed in more conventional frameworks, using only the current molecule and observed feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0, while the quoted molecules contain crowded substituted aza rings, fluorinated saturated carbons and bridged cages. The observed structural diversity therefore leaves configuration unresolved; the supplied scores do not establish whether assigning configuration would be recognized or rewarded.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not demonstrate stereochemically specified alternatives for its asymmetric ring and substituent chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where a generated graph permits stereoisomers, expose chemically consistent stereochemical alternatives and determine through the existing identity and evaluation interfaces whether they remain distinct and score-sensitive. Treat this as missing representation coverage, not evidence that one particular configuration is favorable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports charged_rate 0.0, yet higher-scoring molecules include unacylated cyclic amines and aminomethyl branches. Formal charge is unspecified or neutral in these strings; this observation neither removes their potential basicity nor establishes their state under any experimental condition.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not demonstrate charge-state coverage for the free amines it already emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation could consider chemically appropriate ionization alternatives where the protocol permits them, while checking whether normalization and scoring distinguish those states. No objective identity or presumed assay condition should be used to choose a charge state.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several leading large heterocyclic molecules share the recorded score 0.6155070237050044 despite changes in alkyl length, sulfur substitution and N-bromination. Long ether/thioether appendages and crowded substitutions persist, while other leading families similarly contain many close variants of elaborate ring systems.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not establish which bulky peripheral decorations are dispensable within a high-scoring family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer controlled peripheral shortening or branch replacement that keeps the central attachment framework intact. Observed ties can motivate testing simpler molecules, but do not prove that an unevaluated deletion will preserve the score; retain ordinary feedback-based comparison.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
